Gaming.Boost.Cores.Desc: Disables CPU core parking so frame time stays even without momentary dips.
Gaming.Boost.Cores.Tip: Disables core parking so all CPU cores stay awake — no latency spike on the first hits. If your Windows doesn't expose this setting (Modern Standby systems), the card honestly reports "not available" instead of a red error.
Gaming.Boost.Cores.Title: All CPU cores unparked
Gaming.Boost.Foreground.Desc: Tunes the Windows processor quantum in favor of the foreground app (your game).
Gaming.Boost.Foreground.Tip: Sets Win32PrioritySeparation to 0x26 (38): short time slices with a 3× foreground bias — the game in focus gets far more CPU than background apps.
Gaming.Boost.Foreground.Title: Lowest priority for background apps
Gaming.Boost.GameDvr.Desc: Disables Game DVR background capture so GPU and disk stay free for the game.
Gaming.Boost.GameDvr.Tip: Disables Game Bar background recording and Windows DVR. It occupies the encoder and disk even when you are not recording and causes frame drops.
Gaming.Boost.GameDvr.Title: Game Bar background recording off
Gaming.Boost.Indexing.Desc: Keeps the Windows Search service stopped while this is on; the switch starting again turns the service back on.
Gaming.Boost.Indexing.Tip: Temporarily stops the Windows Search service so it doesn't eat disk/CPU mid-game. Windows search becomes slow until you toggle back, but nothing is deleted.
Gaming.Boost.Indexing.Title: Pause Windows Search indexing (while on)
Gaming.Boost.Keyboard.Desc: Sets keyboard repeat delay to zero and speed to maximum — made for timing-critical keyboard games.
Gaming.Boost.Keyboard.Tip: Sets keyboard repeat delay to shortest and repeat rate to maximum — snappier held-key movement and faster typing. One click restores your previous values.
Gaming.Boost.Keyboard.Title: Faster keyboard repeat
Gaming.Boost.Nagle.Desc: Disables Nagle and delayed ACK on every network adapter so game input is sent immediately.
Gaming.Boost.Nagle.Tip: Nagle's algorithm batches small network packets to save bandwidth — fine for downloads, bad for ping. This disables it (TcpAckFrequency=1 + TCPNoDelay=1) on every network card so each controller input is sent immediately. Restart the game after applying for the full effect.
Gaming.Boost.Nagle.Title: Lower online input delay
Gaming.Boost.Ntfs.Desc: Stops updating the last-access stamp on files to reduce disk writes.
Gaming.Boost.Ntfs.Tip: Disables NTFS last-access timestamp updates, removing an extra disk write on every file read — level loads get faster on both SSD and HDD.
Gaming.Boost.Ntfs.Title: NTFS last-access timestamps off
Gaming.Boost.PerfCounters.Desc: Turns off Perflib counters so the system stops paying a permanent measuring tax.
Gaming.Boost.PerfCounters.Tip: Perflib performance counters are Windows' background measurement services; they cost a little CPU. Some charts (Task Manager → Performance) show no data while active — everything returns when you toggle it off.
Gaming.Boost.PerfCounters.Title: Disable Windows performance counters
Gaming.Boost.Scheduling.Desc: Raises the multimedia scheduling priority of games to the top (GPU, CPU and SFIO).
Gaming.Boost.Scheduling.Tip: Gives Windows' "Games" task category CPU priority 6, GPU priority 8 and High scheduling — while a game runs, the scheduler serves it before background apps.
Gaming.Boost.Scheduling.Title: Maximum scheduling priority for games
Gaming.Boost.Subtitle: Reversible Windows optimizations for smoother frames and lower input lag; every change is journaled and reverts when you flip the switch off.
Gaming.Boost.SysMain.Desc: Keeps the SysMain/SuperFetch service stopped while this is on; turning the switch off starts it again.
Gaming.Boost.SysMain.Tip: Temporarily stops SysMain/SuperFetch (RAM prefetching), freeing memory; usually smoother frames on low-RAM or slow-disk systems. Harmless to revert at any time.
Gaming.Boost.SysMain.Title: SuperFetch off (while on)
Gaming.Boost.Throttling.Desc: Lifts the multimedia packet cap so ping stays stable in busy moments.
Gaming.Boost.Throttling.Tip: While any audio/video plays, Windows throttles network traffic every millisecond, which spikes ping. This removes that limit entirely (0xFFFFFFFF) so your ping stays flat during Discord/streaming.
Gaming.Boost.Throttling.Title: Remove multimedia network throttle
Gaming.Boost.Title: System Boost
Gaming.Boost.Ultimate.Desc: Creates and activates the Windows Ultimate Performance power scheme; flipping it off restores your previous plan.
Gaming.Boost.Ultimate.Tip: Creates (if needed) and activates the Windows Ultimate Performance power plan: the CPU never enters deep sleep and wake-up latency disappears — at higher power draw. Toggling off restores your previous plan.
Gaming.Boost.Ultimate.Title: Ultimate Performance mode

Gaming.Console.PS4.S2: Pick the Windows hotspot Wi-Fi (named after this PC) and enter its password.
Gaming.Console.PS4.S3: Leave everything on Automatic — the hotspot provides IP and DNS.
Gaming.Console.PS4.S4: Run Test Internet Connection — with KOALIX connected you exit through the tunnel.
Gaming.Console.PS4.S5: Keep the hotspot and KOALIX running until you finish playing.

Settings.KillForeignVpnHint: Before every connect, running VPN/proxy clients from the known list (VeePN, v2rayN, Clash, Psiphon, WARP, Windscribe, Lantern, other OpenVPN GUIs …) are closed so they cannot steal the default route or DNS mid-session. KOALIX's own engines are never touched.

Settings.MuxNote: Carries many streams inside one channel — on congested Iranian lines it can improve parallelism and stability. Xray engine only and the server (Xray/V2Ray) must support Mux.Cool; off by default.
Settings.OfficialWireGuard: Full-tunnel WireGuard via official WireGuard for Windows (if installed)
Settings.OpenVpnNote: The official OpenVPN engine. Install from openvpn.net (the official installer also brings the TAP/TUN drivers) or drop openvpn.exe into the engines\openvpn folder.
Settings.PoisonGuardNote: Before every connect the server name is asked from BOTH the system DNS and encrypted DoH (8.8.8.8); when the answers disagree (ISP DNS poisoning) KOALIX dials the DoH-confirmed IP directly while SNI/Host keep the domain — the "works sometimes" lottery ends.
Settings.RevertOnExit: Revert gaming boosts when KOALIX exits
Settings.StrictOffNote: From this version strict routing defaults to OFF — it clashed with other VPNs' WFP filters (WireSock, official WireGuard…). Re-enable it here any time.

Settings.TunCompatNote: If connecting cuts your internet: keep stack on gvisor and try turning strict routing off. Applies on next connect.
Settings.TunMtuNote: 9000 gives the best throughput; if pages hang half-loaded or some sites never open, try 1500 or 1380. Applies on next connect.

Tour.Step1Text: KOALIX is a filter-breaker and a complete network toolbox for Windows: config & subscription management, per-app split tunneling, DNS, ping monitoring, usage reports and gaming optimizations — one bilingual (fa/en) app.
Tour.Step2Text: Settings → Engines installs the cores. sing-box alone is enough to start; add Xray for special configs. WireGuard and OpenVPN live there too — everything downloads from official sources with SHA-256 verification.
Tour.Step3Text: Paste a config or subscription link on the Tunnels page — or drop links and files straight onto the window. Per subscription you can pin the engine (sing-box or Xray) and watch its volume and remaining days right there.
Tour.Step4Text: Don't want your whole connection tunneled? Choose exactly which apps go through the tunnel — everything else stays direct and fast.
Tour.Step5Text: Hit Connect on the dashboard. TUN adapters need administrator rights — if you forgot, the restart-as-administrator button sits right under the warning. Run 'Ping all' first to pick the fastest server.
Tour.Step6Text: Explore the sidebar: DNS manager, Routing Inspector, Ping monitor, Reports, Gaming mode and the Network Repair center. Replay this guide any time from Settings. Enjoy!
Settings.SoundsHint: Pick a built-in sound, “None” or your own wav/mp3 file for each event. Reconnecting, ping-spike and auto-switch sounds play at most once every 12 seconds.

Gaming.Lan.Title: Share the proxy on your home network
Gaming.Lan.Desc: Console or phone on the same modem / Wi-Fi (or this PC's hotspot): in the device's network settings set the HTTP proxy to “this PC's IP” and this port. Only local-network devices are accepted.
Gaming.Lan.PasswordTip: With a password the device must enter any user name and this password. PS5 has no password field — leave it empty for it.
Gaming.Lan.Waiting: On — waiting for KOALIX to connect…
Gaming.Lan.PortInUse: Another program holds this port; pick a different one.
Gaming.Lan.BadPort: The port must be a number between 1025 and 65535.
Gaming.Lan.Udp: The proxy carries TCP only (store, downloads, web, sign-in); online-game UDP traffic does not go through it — use the hotspot way for that. Xbox has no proxy setting.
About.Title: About KOALIX
About.Tagline: Smart tunnelling, low ping, full control — in one app.
About.Description: KOALIX is an all-in-one connection manager for Windows: it drives sing-box, Xray, WireGuard and WireSock from one place, splits traffic smartly, manages DNS and keeps your ping low for gaming.
About.F1Text: sing-box, Xray, WireGuard and WireSock with automatic best-server pick.
About.F2Text: Only the apps and sites you choose go through the tunnel.
About.F3Text: Auto game detection, network boosts and a live ping monitor.
About.F4Text: Fast, secure DNS with benchmarks and automatic revert.
About.F5Text: See which route and engine every connection takes.
About.F6Text: Neon/Minimal/Retro styles, glass mode, reactive ARGB and a floating widget.
About.MadeWith: Made with ❤ on .NET and WPF — for a freer internet and a lower ping.

Settings.WidgetTempHint: CPU/GPU and GPU hotspot temperatures come from HWiNFO (with Shared Memory on) or MSI Afterburner when running; otherwise from Windows' own sensors (which may not cover everything).

Tour.Step7Text: A tiny always-on-top overlay like MSI Afterburner: ping, speed, CPU and GPU temps, even the GPU hotspot. Turn it on in Settings, switch its mode, fade it or lock it — its × closes it.
Tour.Step8Text: Make a profile per game and tick Auto: when the game starts, KOALIX switches on network boosts, low ping and focus mode, and reverts them after you quit.
Tour.Step9Text: Pick the Neon, Minimal or Retro style in Settings, turn on glass mode and make ARGB reactive so the colours spin with your download speed or ping.
Tour.Step10Text: Ctrl+Alt+K connects/disconnects without opening the window. Ctrl+K is quick search, and the tray icon gives you servers, the widget and settings.

Guide.AddConfig.Title: How do I add a config?
Guide.AddConfig.Body:
1. On the Dashboard press the + button (bottom of the page), or open Tunnels from the sidebar.
2. Copy your config link and paste it into the box at the top. You can paste several links at once, one per line.
3. Press Import.

Tip: you can also drag a config file or link text straight onto the KOALIX window.
Guide.Connect.Title: How do I connect?
Guide.Connect.Body:
1. On the Dashboard pick a server from the list (or choose "Auto — best server" to let KOALIX pick the fastest).
2. Press the big button in the middle.
3. When the button changes colour and says Connected, you're done.

Press the same button again to disconnect. You can also connect or disconnect from the KOALIX icon next to the Windows clock.
Guide.Ping.Title: What is ping, and which server is best?
Guide.Ping.Body:
Ping is the round-trip time to a server, in milliseconds. Lower is faster.

• Under 150: excellent
• 150 – 400: fine
• Over 400 or "error": slow or unreachable

Press "Ping all" on the Dashboard and pick the server with the lowest ping.
Guide.Subs.Title: What is a subscription link?
Guide.Subs.Body:
A subscription is an https address from your provider that holds a list of several servers.

1. Paste the subscription address on the Tunnels page like any other config and press Import.
2. All of its servers are added at once.
3. KOALIX refreshes subscriptions automatically, so when your provider changes servers you don't have to do anything.
Guide.Split.Title: What is split tunneling?
Guide.Split.Body:
It lets you decide which apps go through the tunnel and which connect to the internet directly.

• Full tunnel: every app goes through the tunnel (simplest).
• Only selected apps: e.g. just the browser and Telegram.
• All except selected: e.g. everything except a game or a banking app.

Pick the mode on the Split Tunneling page and add your apps.
Guide.Modes.Title: Beginner or Advanced?
Guide.Modes.Body:
The title bar has a "Beginner | Advanced" switch.

• Beginner: expert pages and options are hidden so only what you need is in front of you.
• Advanced: every tool — DNS, Gaming, Ping Monitor, System Proxy, Logs, the map and charts.

Switching never deletes or disables a setting; it only simplifies what you see.
Guide.Tray.Title: The tray icon and widget
Guide.Tray.Body:
When you close the KOALIX window, it keeps running in the notification area next to the Windows clock.

• Click the icon for the quick panel: connect, disconnect and switch servers.
• To quit completely, right-click the icon and choose Exit.
• Ctrl+Alt+K connects or disconnects from anywhere in Windows.
Guide.Map.Title: Map and charts
Guide.Map.Body:
In Advanced mode the Dashboard shows a server map (flat 2D or a 3D globe), a speed chart, a latency chart and per-app usage.

Rotate the globe with W A S D or by dragging, and zoom with the mouse wheel.
Guide.Gaming.Title: Gaming
Guide.Gaming.Body:
The Gaming page helps reduce lag in games.

1. Pick or add your game.
2. Choose system optimisations (such as Windows Game Mode and a higher priority for the game) and press Apply.
3. Every change is reversible — the previous values are saved.

This page is only visible in Advanced mode; the button below switches for you.
Guide.Dns.Title: DNS Manager
Guide.Dns.Body:
DNS is the internet's phone book: it turns a site name into an IP address. A good DNS is faster and protects against DNS poisoning.

On the DNS Manager page you can test several DNS servers and apply the fastest. If you're not sure, keep the default.
Guide.NoConnect.Title: It won't connect
Guide.NoConnect.Body:
1. Test the pings — the selected server may be down. Try another one.
2. Make sure an engine is installed (Settings › Engines).
3. If you use a subscription, refresh it; the servers may have changed.
4. Still stuck? Open Network Repair, run System self-check first, then the suggested operations.
Guide.Slow.Title: The internet is slow
Guide.Slow.Body:
1. Press "Ping all" and pick the server with the lowest ping.
2. If only a few apps need the tunnel, turn on split tunneling so everything else connects directly.
3. Try "Auto — best server" so KOALIX picks the fastest one and switches if it fails.
Guide.NoInternet.Title: No internet after disconnecting or closing the app
Guide.NoInternet.Body:
After a sudden shutdown, Windows proxy or DNS settings sometimes don't get restored.

Open Network Repair and run System self-check. Each operation (such as restoring the proxy or DNS) is fully explained and only runs after you confirm it.
Guide.EngineMissing.Title: "Engine not found"
Guide.EngineMissing.Body:
sing-box or Xray isn't installed yet, or your antivirus removed it.

Open Settings › Engines and press Install / update. If the antivirus deletes it again, add the KOALIX folder as an exception.
Guide.Admin.Title: Why does it ask for Administrator?
Guide.Admin.Body:
Creating the tunnel adapter (TUN mode) and changing Windows network routes requires admin rights.

When the UAC prompt appears, press Yes. KOALIX only changes its own network settings and restores them all when you disconnect.
Guide.SubFail.Title: A subscription won't refresh
Guide.SubFail.Body:
1. Open the subscription link in a browser. If it doesn't open there either, it has expired — ask your provider for a new one.
2. If the link only opens through a tunnel, connect to a server first, then refresh.
3. If the link changed, delete the old subscription and import the new link.
